title: Meeting Rooms II
pattern: Sort by start + min-heap of end times
statement: Given the `[start, end]` times of meetings, return the **minimum number of rooms** needed so that no two meetings in the same room overlap.

example.why: [0, 30] occupies one room the whole time; [5, 10] and [15, 20] can share a second room.

idea: Handle the meetings in order of **start time**. When a meeting starts, the only question is: has some room become free by now?
Keep a **min-heap of end times**, one entry per room in use. Its top is the room that frees up first — if even that one is still busy, every room is.
If the earliest-ending room is free (its end ≤ this start), reuse it: pop its end time. Either way push this meeting's end time. The heap's size at the end is the number of rooms.

complexity.timeWhy: Sorting, plus one heap push/pop per meeting.
complexity.spaceWhy: The heap can hold one end time per meeting.

steps.text: Our example: **`intervals = [[0,30],[15,20],[5,10]]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Sort the meetings by start time, so they are handled in the order they begin.
The first meeting [0, 30] takes a room. The heap stores, for each room in use, **when its meeting ends** — the top is the room that frees up first.

steps.text: Meeting [5, 10] starts at 5, but even the room that frees up first is busy until 30. A **new room** is needed.

steps.text: This meeting's room is now busy until 10. Rooms in use: **2**.

views.title: min_heap  (end time of the meeting in each room)

steps.text: Meeting [15, 20] starts at 15. The earliest room is free from 10 — in time. **Reuse that room.**

views.title: min_heap  (end time of the meeting in each room)

steps.text: This meeting's room is now busy until 20. Rooms in use: **2**.

views.title: min_heap  (end time of the meeting in each room)

steps.text: Every meeting has a room. Rooms needed: **2**.

views.title: min_heap  (end time of the meeting in each room)

steps.text: Done — the answer is **`2`**. [0, 30] occupies one room the whole time; [5, 10] and [15, 20] can share a second room.
